subject: review:Z014
looked_at: trench-warfare-3d/Tools/assetboard/ops.py (335-370, the runs' reading), Tools/toolcheck.py (9-33), Tools/assetboard/briefs.py (68-170, the brief's own checks)
docs/reference/tasks.md and docs/reference/decisions.md (grep only: the 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 rows)

tasks.title: The run reader's own example is refused by its tool
tasks.why: P1. runreport.py:68 refuses the word "lands" (HIS = landed|lands|merged) in the title, --did, --left and every unit sentence, but the skill the agent follows shows exactly that word in its model example: .claude/skills/tw-run-report/SKILL.md:41 ("lands them on the far bank") and :43 ("carries two tanks across and lands them"). SKILL.md:62 announces only "landed" and "merged", so the agent has no warning. An agent that copies the shape it was given is refused and must rewrite inside a 20-minute, $2 reading; and a normal game sentence (a ferry lands a tank, troops landed on the bank) cannot be written at all.
tasks.done_when: a new case in test_runs.py feeds the skill's own example words to runreport.check() and gets no refusal, and the existing case 'report: "landed" and "merged" are refused wherever they stand' still passes; python Tools/assetboard/test_runs.py exits 0

tasks.title: A brief's own words are never checked for code
tasks.why: P2. check() at runreport.py:268 scans only the title, --did, --left and the unit sentences for file names, backticks and "landed" (CODE at :70, HIS at :68). The brief the same agent writes for the owner goes through brief() at :364 into briefs.add(), which caps words (briefs.py:108) and checks nothing else, so a brief's title, --for, --option and --why may carry a file name, a backtick or a finding tag straight onto his Decide page. That is the one page where the plain-words rule matters most, and the skill (SKILL.md:63, 108) tells the agent the tool checks the words.
tasks.done_when: a case in test_runs.py writes a brief whose title or --for names a .cs file and is refused with that reason, and the plain brief of the existing case is still written; python Tools/assetboard/test_runs.py exits 0

tasks.title: Without node, the page's forty-odd cases silently pass
tasks.why: P2. test_runs.py:497 and :579 look for node with shutil.which and, when it is missing, print a line and return; every case of page_rules() (:532-561) and drawn() (:601-610) is then never added to `results`, and the run still exits 0 at :629. toolcheck.py:33 runs each Tools/**/test_*.py as the only guard a tool lane has, and nothing else reads runs.js or runsboard.js, so on a station or a CI shell without node the whole Runs page is unguarded while the gate reports green.
tasks.done_when: with node hidden from PATH, python Tools/assetboard/test_runs.py exits non-zero and names the missing node as a failed case; with node present it exits 0

tasks.title: The Drive going away at a reading's end wedges the watcher
tasks.why: P2. finish() at runreport.py:520-530 appends the reading's line with where.mkdir() and open(...,'a') outside any try, and deletes state()/running.json only afterwards. G:/My Drive is the folder (build.py:40), so if it is away when a reading ends the OSError leaves running.json in place; ops.py:364 catches it and src_runs.failed() blanks the Runs page to "could not be read" on every watch cycle, and the next tick tries the same finish again. Nothing in the module's own Drive-away guard (runreport.py tick, the DRIVE_WAS line) covers the end of a reading.
tasks.done_when: a case in test_runs.py ends a reading with the reports folder made unwritable and finish() returns, running.json is gone and the next tick starts a reading again; python Tools/assetboard/test_runs.py exits 0
